description: A two-panel composite figure of grouped horizontal bar charts reporting the yield stress at 650 °C of Fe–Al–M–C alloys tested in compression and in tension. Both panels share the same x-axis, labelled "Yield stress [MPa]", running 0–450 with tick marks every 50 MPa; each panel has its own legend giving dark grey = "(in compression)" and light grey = "(in tension)". Panel (a) ranks five Fe–15Al based alloys top to bottom: Fe-15Al, Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-15Al-2V-1C, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C and Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C. Panel (b) ranks seven Fe–26Al based alloys: Fe-26Al, Fe-26Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-2V-1C, Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C and Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C. In every alloy pair the dark compression bar is longer than its light tension partner, so the compressive yield stress always exceeds the tensile yield stress — the tension–compression asymmetry the figure exists to demonstrate. The largest values belong to the Nb- and Ta-bearing alloys, whose compression bars reach the 300–450 MPa region, whereas the binary Fe-15Al and Fe-26Al bars stay close to the 100 MPa tick. No numeric value labels are printed on the bars.

observations.observation: Both panels are grouped horizontal bar charts whose shared x-axis is labelled 'Yield stress [MPa]' and runs from 0 to 450 in 50 MPa intervals.
Each panel carries a legend defining dark grey bars as '(in compression)' and light grey bars as '(in tension)'.
Panel (a) contains five alloy labels read top to bottom: Fe-15Al, Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-15Al-2V-1C, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C.
Panel (b) contains seven alloy labels read top to bottom: Fe-26Al, Fe-26Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-2V-1C, Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C.
For every alloy pair in both panels the dark compression bar is longer than the light tension bar, i.e. the compressive yield stress is higher than the tensile yield stress.

In panel (a) the longest bars are those of Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C and Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C, whose compression bars extend into the 400–450 MPa region of the axis, while the binary Fe-15Al bars end just past the 100 MPa tick.

In panel (b) Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C has the longest compression bar (ending between the 300 and 350 MPa ticks) and Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C the second longest; the binary Fe-26Al bars are the shortest, ending between the 100 and 150 MPa ticks.
No numeric values are printed on the bars; all magnitudes can only be read against the 50 MPa gridline intervals.
The caption states that the figure shows yield stresses at 650 °C in compression and in tension for Fe–15Al based (a) and Fe–26Al-based (b) alloys.
The citing text states that alloys were tested in tension at 650 and 800 °C because room-temperature testing revealed significant tension–compression asymmetry.

The citing text states that the comparison of yield stress in compression and in tension at 650 °C (Fig. 7) and at 800 °C (Fig. 8) confirms the asymmetric tension–compression behaviour of all investigated alloys at both temperatures.

The maximum compressive yield stresses occur for the Nb- and Ta-containing alloys in both panels, while the V-containing alloys give intermediate compression bars (between roughly the 150 and 250 MPa ticks).

subfigures.description: Grouped horizontal bar chart for five Fe–15Al based alloys (Fe-15Al, Fe-15Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-15Al-2V-1C, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C), x-axis 'Yield stress [MPa]' 0–450 in 50 MPa steps; legend dark grey '(in compression)', light grey '(in tension)'. In every alloy the compression bar exceeds the tension bar; the largest bars are the Nb- and Ta-containing alloys reaching the 350–450 MPa region, the binary Fe-15Al bars sit just above the 100 MPa tick.

Grouped horizontal bar chart for seven Fe–26Al based alloys (Fe-26Al, Fe-26Al-2Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-4Ti-1C, Fe-26Al-2V-1C, Fe-26Al-2Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C, Fe-26Al-2Ta-1C), same x-axis 'Yield stress [MPa]' 0–450 in 50 MPa steps and same compression/tension legend. Compression again exceeds tension for every alloy; Fe-26Al-4Nb-1C shows the longest compression bar (between the 300 and 350 MPa ticks) and the binary Fe-26Al the shortest bars.
